title: How to Recover When You Miss an Internal Deadline
summary: Missed an IB internal deadline in DP2? Learn what to do in the first 24 hours, contact the right people, rebuild your plan, and submit safely.
body_markdown:
Missing an internal deadline in the **IB DP2 fall term** is serious, but it is not automatically irreversible. Contact the relevant teacher immediately, submit the most complete work you currently have, confirm the school policy, and propose a short, realistic completion plan.


September to November can be difficult because IAs, the Extended Essay, TOK, predicted-grade assessments, university applications, and new content often overlap. Your priority is to establish what was missed, protect your eligibility for assessment, and restore a workable schedule.


### Identify which deadline you missed


The term **internal deadline** can describe several stages. A missed planning checkpoint does not necessarily have the same consequences as a missed final submission date.


Deadline type What it usually means Immediate priority


Planning checkpoint A proposal, question, outline, method, or source list was due Send available planning evidence and request a revised checkpoint


Complete draft The teacher expected a version for permitted feedback Submit the current version and ask whether feedback remains available


Final school deadline Work was due for marking, authentication, or processing Contact the teacher and DP coordinator immediately


School upload stage The school is preparing work or marks for IB submission Follow the coordinator's instructions urgently


The IB does not publish one universal student-facing deadline for every school. For components such as the **Extended Essay** and **TOK** , IB submission requirements lead schools to establish earlier internal schedules. Your coordinator calendar and school policy therefore remain authoritative, even when an online IB date appears later.


Missing an early checkpoint may reduce the feedback available. Missing a final deadline can be more serious because the school needs time to authenticate work, mark components, standardize marks, and manage submission procedures.
